hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation of the product as built
hard_gates.evidence:
No leak found.

API attack (attacks/g1-attack.mjs, g1-a-vs-b.txt): alnoor's admin made 1,049 judged calls against gulfsteel. They covered:
- every identity, auth, list-view and report route in the OpenAPI, with each of 30 B ids (users, roles, companies, tenant, canary user and role);
- B ids in body fields (roleIds, companyRoles, companyId, userIds, filter, search);
- ?removePasskeys=true and ?passkeyId=;
- the tenant-switch headers X-Tenant, X-Tenant-Id, X-Erp-Tenant and X-Workspace, and tenant/workspace query fields;
- users and roles exports as CSV, XLSX and PDF in English and Arabic, and both identity reports.
No B secret appeared in any body or header. Every B-id call answered 404, or a 400 that was identical for B ids, random ids and A ids (oracle.txt). A hash of B's identity state was the same before and after.

'All that match' with B's addresses or B's filter answered 409 'changed (1 then, 0 now)', and nothing in B changed (bulk.txt).

The new sign-in pause (pause.txt, pause2.txt):
- An attacker's 7 failures answer the same sequence (401 x4, then 429 with Retry-After) for an unknown address, a B-only address, an address in both tenants and a deactivated B account.
- The owner, from their own browser (device cookie), still signs in with 200 after the attack.
- The admin's history shows the paused client, and Unblock lifts it (204, then 200).

Database, as erp_app (db-app-role.txt):
- No tenant bound: 0 rows. Bound to A: 100,004 users, 0 from another tenant.
- UPDATE of B's users changed 0 rows. INSERTs into B's sign_in_attempts and user_roles were refused by RLS.
- The new platform tables sign_in_failures and sign_in_secret are refused to erp_app (permission denied).
- verify_sign_in returns nothing inside a tenant-bound transaction.
- row_security=off, SET ROLE erp_owner/erp_auth and DISABLE RLS were all refused. No erp role has bypassrls.
- Every identity tenant table has RLS enabled and forced.

hard_gates.gate: G1 gate catches tenant leaks planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence:
Plants are in plants/apply-r10-plants.py and r10-plants.diff.

L1: a process-wide memo in SignInService of each address's pause end, keyed by address only. Caught by G1ProcessStateTests ('static ...SignInService.PauseMemo: a read-only field that holds a mutable ConcurrentDictionary') and by G1SignInThrottleTests (the owner's own client answered 429) (plants/run1/dotnet-suite.log).

L2: identity.verify_sign_in answers the workspace of the first account with the address instead of the one whose password matched, so a B password opens A. Run alone (plants/run-L2): caught by G1SignInThrottleTests.Failed_sign_ins_from_one_client_never_lock_the_account_out_for_anyone_else ('Expected bravo..., Actual alpha'). It is caught on every run whatever the salt order, because the gate signs in with both tenants' passwords. AuthTests also catches it.

G2 gate catches missing permission checks planted in this piece's surface
hard_gates.evidence:
Server plants:
- S1 (round 9's P4 again: RevokeSessions skips the target check when removePasskeys=true). Run alone (plants/run-S1), G2AccountTakeoverTests.Acting_on_a_user_needs_every_permission_that_user_holds fails. - S3 (PUT default-company skips the target check). Caught by Acting_on_a_record_that_grants_access_needs_everything_it_grants (13 lines, 'answered 200 (expected 403)').
- S4 (DELETE passkeys?passkeyId= skips the target check). Run alone (plants/run-S4), caught cleanly: 'passkeyId=7bf9... aimed at the Administrator ... answered 200 (expected 403)' and 'the Administrator's passkeys changed'.

Screen plants (plants/web-planted.log):
- U2 (the palette's Sign out everywhere without allowed.signOutEverywhere) is caught by paletteActions.test.tsx.
- U3 (the palette's Delete role without actions.delete) is caught: 'Delete role sent DELETE /api/identity/roles/r-clerk'.
- U1 (the palette's 'Allow sign-in again' without requires signIns.read) is not caught (web-U1-only.log: 479 passed). It is not counted as a permission miss, because the role does allow unblock (POST /unblock needs identity.users.update only). It is a dead-end entry; see other findings.

biggest_gap.title: The permission matrix shrinks every 'Other' permission's checkbox to a dot, so the most sensitive grants are the hardest to see and click when building a restricted role
biggest_gap.detail:
In Roles, the matrix's 'Other' column holds the permissions that are not view, create, change or delete. Today these are 'Reset other users' passwords' and 'Share list views with everyone'. As modules arrive, this column will hold post journal, approve, close period and the like.

There, the checkbox renders 4.5 to 11.8 px wide, against 13 px for every other checkbox. It looks like a list bullet ('◦'), not a box, at every common screen width. In the system Administrator role, the ticked state is almost invisible.

An administrator setting up a 'Sales clerk' or 'Storekeeper' role in a UAE trading or manufacturing company cannot see at a glance whether the risky grants are on. With a mouse they must hit a target a few pixels wide. Odoo's group and access screens show such rights as ordinary full-size toggles.

Keyboard toggling works (Space), and the API is correct. So this is the screen failing the 'dense, Dynamics-style business screen' promise exactly where the stakes are highest.

Cause: web/src/modules/identity/identity.css, .id-cell is display:inline-flex. The checkbox keeps the default flex-shrink:1 and is squeezed when the label beside it wraps.

Fix: give the checkbox flex: 0 0 auto (or put the label under it). Add a screen test that every matrix checkbox renders at full size at 1280, 1600 and 1920 px.
biggest_gap.evidence:
1. ./erp up. Sign in as admin@alnoor.example. Press G then R and open 'Administrator', or press Alt+N.
2. Look at the 'Users' row, 'Other' column ('Reset other users' passwords'), or at 'List views'.
3. Measure, as walks/other.mjs and walks/other2.mjs do: page.getByRole('checkbox',{name:"Reset other users' passwords"}).evaluate(e=>e.getBoundingClientRect().width) gives 5.17 at 1280 px wide, 5.75 at 1600, 7.77 at 1920 and 11.78 at 2560. 'View users' gives 13 at every width.

Screenshot: 03-matrix-other-column-checkbox-1920-en.png. The same in Arabic: 10-new-role-matrix-ar.jpg ('إعادة تعيين كلمات مرور المستخدمين الآخرين' with a dot). Widths are in walks/matrix-other-checkbox-widths.txt.

other_findings: Unblocking from a user's own record leaves that record stale. The administrator opens a paused user, goes to Sign-in history and presses 'Allow sign-in again' (button or palette). Their next save in the same record (for example unticking Active) is refused with 'Someone else changed this record after you opened it. Reload it and try again.' Nobody else changed it: the unblock bumped the user's version, and the form kept the old one. The deactivation is lost until they reload and redo it. 'Sign out everywhere' followed by a save works. Repro: walks/deact2.mjs; screenshot 11-own-unblock-then-save-refused-en.jpg.

No gate covers a palette action's 'requires' list. Removing requires: ["identity.signIns.read"] from the palette's 'Allow sign-in again' (web/src/modules/identity/extensions.ts) leaves all 479 web unit tests green (plants/web-U1-only.log). A user with identity.users.update but no sign-in history permission is then offered an entry that opens a tab they cannot see. It is not a permission leak (the role does allow POST /unblock), but the palette gate's builder plants (PA1 to PA10) never test 'requires'.

When S1 is planted, the main takeover gate fails by a 401 crash, not a report. AimQueriesAsync's query variant ends the Administrator's session, and the gate's next read at G2AccountTakeoverTests.cs line 287 throws before the 'Administrator's session ended' check further down can name the endpoint. The fault is still caught, but a builder sees 'Response status code does not indicate success: 401' instead of the endpoint and query that did it. Check the session first, or catch the 401 and report it.

The palette's record commands follow the open tab. With a user open on 'What they can do', Ctrl+K offers no 'Reset password…' (in either language). On Details it does. This matches the buttons, but a keyboard user must switch tabs first.
A copied role is named 'X (copy)' in English but 'X (2)' in Arabic (screenshots 07 and 10).

Ours' all-keyboard path for create-restricted-user (9 steps, 46 keys) still ties Odoo's 46 keystrokes; only the pointer path wins. Typed-name find-user paths (21 and 15 keys) lose to Odoo's 5 keystrokes; only the initials path wins.

Critic housekeeping: my DELETE probe in attacks/oracle.mjs removed tenant A's never-signed-in demo user admin.ar@alnoor.example from my own demo copy. That was allowed by design, and the audit trail named the actor. My demo was torn down afterwards; the shared product is unaffected.
